findings: Direct access to the Reuters March 27 report establishes that Rubio said the State Department may have revoked more than 300 visas and confirmed Ozturk's visa revocation; the total remains qualified and combines student and visitor visas.

Independent AP reporting establishes the March 25 detention, reports counsel said no charges had been filed, and describes Ozturk's prior Tufts Daily opinion piece. Neither source establishes that all revocations were triggered by Israel criticism or social-media posts.

The proposal replaces the unsupported DHS/blanket-causation and March 1 date claims with a dated account of Rubio's announcement and the named case. It distinguishes reported actions from unresolved individual grounds and uses no process filler.

full_corrected_proposal.title: Rubio Reports More Than 300 Visa Revocations, Confirms Ozturk Visa Action
full_corrected_proposal.description_short: Rubio said the State Department may have revoked over 300 visas and confirmed Tufts student Rumeysa Ozturk's visa revocation; he gave no case-specific reason.
full_corrected_proposal.description_medium: At a March 27, 2025, press event in Guyana, Secretary of State Marco Rubio said the State Department may have revoked more than 300 visas, including student and visitor visas, and said he signed each action. He confirmed Tufts doctoral student Rumeysa Ozturk's visa was revoked but did not explain her specific conduct. Independent reporting describes her arrest and prior campus opinion writing, not a general Israel-criticism trigger.
full_corrected_proposal.description_long: On March 27, 2025, Secretary of State Marco Rubio said the State Department may have revoked more than 300 visas. He described the total as including student and visitor visas and said he had signed each action. He made the remarks in Guyana after federal agents detained Tufts University doctoral student Rumeysa Ozturk and the State Department revoked her visa. The Associated Press reported that Ozturk's lawyer said no charges had been filed. AP also reported that she was one of four students who wrote a Tufts Daily opinion piece criticizing the university's response to demands for divestment from companies tied to Israel. Reuters reported Rubio did not explain what specific conduct by Ozturk justified revoking her visa. He listed vandalism, harassment, building takeovers and other disruptive conduct as grounds for taking away student visas, but did not say Ozturk had done those things. He said the standard in her case involved support for movements contrary to U.S. foreign policy. The reporting does not show that every visa in the reported total was revoked for criticism of Israel, for a social media post, or for one common reason; it leaves individual grounds unresolved.

The reporting does not establish the individual grounds for each revocation or that every action concerned criticism of Israel, a social-media post, or the same conduct.

impact_proposal.confidence_reason: Reuters directly reports Rubio's statement and a named visa revocation; AP independently reports the detention and related case facts. The aggregate remains qualified and individual grounds are unresolved.
impact_proposal.rationale: Visa revocations and one student's detention are consequential but bounded actions; the reported aggregate is qualified and case-specific grounds are unresolved. The evidence does not establish a legal violation, institutional impairment, or private benefit.
